text:
Mitch Marner's second season in Vegas looks like the familiar Marner with the goals missing. He has 23 assists and 27 points in 23 games, 12 of them on the power play, but only four goals.

Our numbers say the goals are the unlucky part. He has 4 on 6.6 expected (expected goals measure chance quality), shooting 6.9% against a talent range centred near 12.7%, and his own chances are up from last season: 0.83 expected goals per 60 against 0.62. With him on the ice at 5v5, Vegas has 55.9% of the expected goals. Goals tend to follow looks like that.

He scored in Winnipeg on Nov. 21, his second goal in ten games. Over that stretch he has 12 points against 12 expected, so the playmaking is right on schedule even as the finishing lags.

The passing is the heart of his game. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.2 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 83rd percentile among forwards, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 16th among 401 forwards at 2.9 wins above replacement.
